headline: Oil Set for Third Weekly Drop as Ample Supply Counters Iran Risk
author: Kanoko Matsuyama

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:05 PM PST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Oil edged higher after a volatile session on Thursday, with futures on track for a third weekly decline as traders weigh the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran against signs of ample supply.
The most-active contract for West Texas Intermediate traded near $83 a barrel after swinging in a range of more than $2 in the previous session, while Brent settled near $92.

US President Donald Trump told Axios he was "not rushing into any decision" on Iran, while Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Fox News played down concerns about regional supplies, saying flows through the Strait of Hormuz reached a record. The comments tempered concerns after Western officials said that the chances of the US launching another round of mass strikes against Iran had risen in recent days.

Global benchmark Brent has retreated about a fifth this month, as supplies from the Middle East recovered and Trump held off on renewed strikes. Still, there's been a flare-up in low-level fighting across the region in recent days, including a spate of attacks on vessels transiting the critical Strait of Hormuz and strikes by Tehran-backed Houthis in Riyadh.

"While the near-term rise in geopolitical tensions is bringing some buying back to crude, the overall fundamentals are still moving more bearish," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president for trading at BOK Financial Securities Inc., pointing to Iraq selling physical crude at steep discounts.

Elsewhere, the leaders of the US, China and Russia agreed to "increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations" at a meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, according to a joint statement. They didn't spell out what that would entail.
